frontmatter.doctitle: Energy in Our Community: A Field Guide

level1.p: Energy makes change possible. A moving bicycle has kinetic energy. A book resting on a high shelf has gravitational potential energy because of its position.

level2.p: Electricity can be generated in several ways. Solar panels convert light into electrical energy. Wind turbines transfer energy from moving air to a generator. Hydroelectric stations use moving water. Each method has benefits and limits.
Choose three devices in a classroom. Record the device, its power rating in watts, and the estimated hours of use each day.
Energy use can be estimated with the equation E = P × t. Here, E is energy in watt-hours, P is power in watts, and t is time in hours.
Calculate the daily energy estimate for each device. Explain why the highest-power device does not always use the most energy.
